clue.text: It left damage in extremely treacherous hot coastal wetland

indicators.note: the damage sits inside the edge letters, which wrap around it

parts.note: 'it' is old slang for sex appeal, abbreviated SA
standard abbreviation for left

indicators.note: something taken to extremes goes to its far ends, so only the first and last letters of the next word count

parts.note: the two end letters of the word
to mar is to damage or spoil
H for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A storm has left wreckage in a scorching, dangerous stretch of coastal marsh.
explanation.walkthrough: SA + L, then T(MAR)S, then H gives SALT MARSH. 'It' meaning sex appeal (SA) is a long-standing crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A salt marsh is low land by the sea flooded by tides, a classic type of coastal wetland.

clue.text: Brother and uncles initially laugh with excitement

parts.note: informal short form of brother

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word just before it

parts.note: first letter of the word
the sound of a laugh written out

explanation.surface: A family gathering where the brother and uncles start laughing excitedly.
explanation.definitionFit: A brouhaha is a noisy fuss or commotion, a state of public excitement.

clue.text: Grief overwhelming young male champion

indicators.note: to overwhelm something is to engulf it, so the first word surrounds the second

parts.note: grief and pain are both forms of suffering
a lad is a boy or young man

explanation.surface: Sorrow crushing a young man who is a sporting champion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overwhelming' reads as describing grief's force, but here it means surrounding.
explanation.definitionFit: A paladin was one of Charlemagne's knights, hence any heroic defender or champion of a cause.

clue.text: Small enough to try

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
ample means plenty, more than enough

explanation.surface: A portion just big enough to taste, like a free sample at a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads like a description of a tasting portion, which is exactly what the answer is.
explanation.definitionFit: To sample is to taste or test something, so it can stand in for 'to try'.

clue.text: Fine sprightly elf-like creature

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
airy can mean light-hearted and lively

explanation.surface: A delicate, lively little sprite of folklore.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairy is a small magical being of folklore, very close in kind to an elf.

clue.text: Girl getting a passage back finally to Caicos Islands

parts.note: informal word for a girl
taken as written

indicators.note: going back means the word for passage is read from right to left

parts.note: a gap is an opening or passage through something

indicators.note: finally picks out the closing letter of each of the two words that follow it

parts.note: last letter of the word
last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A girl books a return trip that ends up in the Turks and Caicos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caicos' tempts you to look in the Caribbean, but the definition is just 'Islands'; the answer is a Pacific archipelago.
explanation.definitionFit: The Galapagos are a group of volcanic Pacific islands belonging to Ecuador.

clue.text: Like a giraffe's day aboard a vessel

definitions.note: adjective: of the kind belonging to a giraffe, i.e. from Africa

indicators.note: in a down clue, being aboard means sitting on top, so the day is placed above the vessel

parts.note: taken as written
short form of Friday
a can is a container or vessel

explanation.surface: A giraffe's day out on board a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Giraffes live wild only in Africa, so something like a giraffe's homeland or origin is African.

clue.text: Frank in love with writer

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: Someone called Frank has fallen for an author.
explanation.walkthrough: Frank looks like a man's name, but it is the adjective meaning candid.
explanation.definitionFit: Being open means being honest and candid, which is what frank means.

clue.text: Duck kept in freezer overnight

indicators.note: kept in says the letters are held inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A duck left in the freezer overnight before cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a score of nothing; the bird in the freezer is a decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: A batsman out without scoring makes a duck, so duck means a score of nought.

clue.text: A dry summer month to go topless and acclimatise

indicators.note: losing its top means the month's opening letter is removed

parts.note: taken as written
TT stands for teetotal, someone who stays dry
a month of the northern summer

explanation.surface: Sunbathing topless in a dry June to get used to the heat.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests sunbathing, but 'topless' just strips JUNE of its J.
explanation.definitionFit: To attune is to adjust or adapt to conditions, the same sense as acclimatising.

clue.text: Despair brewing about jetBlue's latest flight rate

indicators.note: about means around, so the mixed letters surround the single letter
something brewing is being stirred up, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: the letters to be mixed

indicators.note: the latest is the last one, so only the final letter is used

parts.note: last letter of the airline's name

explanation.surface: Passengers despairing over a delayed JetBlue flight, a US budget airline.
explanation.definitionFit: Airspeed is an aircraft's speed relative to the air, the rate at which it flies.

clue.text: Corn I am cooking with a variety of pasta

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: letters to be rearranged
taken as written and added to the mix

explanation.surface: A cook explaining they are making a dish of corn with pasta.
explanation.walkthrough: The article 'a' joins the letters of 'Corn I am' before they are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Macaroni is one particular type of short tubular pasta.

clue.text: Munch cold cut

parts.note: C for cold, as on a tap
to hew is to cut with blows

explanation.surface: Eating a slice of cold meat.
explanation.definitionFit: To munch is to eat steadily with the jaws, which is chewing.

clue.text: Scrap thin broken part of helmet

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so the letters are reassembled differently

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A worn, thin, broken piece of a helmet ready to be thrown away.
explanation.definitionFit: A chinstrap is the band under the jaw that holds a helmet in place.

clue.text: Catches second criminal near back of buildings

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second

indicators.note: criminal suggests something bent or wrong, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter

parts.note: last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Police catch a second offender lurking behind some buildings.
explanation.definitionFit: Snares are traps, and to snare something is to catch it, so snares means catches.

clue.text: Old containers in the kitchen holding last of grilled mushrooms

parts.note: ex means former or old

indicators.note: holding means the kitchen containers wrap around the single letter

parts.note: pans are cooking vessels

indicators.note: the last of a word is its closing letter

parts.note: last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Old kitchen pans full of grilled mushrooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mushrooms' looks like food for the grill, but it is the verb meaning grows fast.
explanation.definitionFit: To mushroom is to grow or spread rapidly, so mushrooms means expands.

clue.text: Some song regularly sung at church

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: first and third letters of the word
taken as written
CH is the standard abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A hymn sung at a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some song' reads like part of the surface, but it is the definition, and 'song' is not the word the letters come from.
explanation.definitionFit: A snatch is a short fragment of a tune, a bit of a song heard or sung briefly.

clue.text: Where food might be fixed, needing small pot on the counter

indicators.note: needing means lacking, so the size abbreviation for small is taken away

parts.note: stable means firmly fixed in place

indicators.note: counter means opposite or contrary, so the word runs the other way

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cooking scene: a small pot set firmly on the kitchen counter.
explanation.walkthrough: STABLE minus S gives TABLE; S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small. 'Counter' looks like a kitchen surface but signals reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Meals are served and set down on the surface of a table, the tabletop.

clue.text: Leader recalled agent in capital city

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the combined letters are read backwards
in places the agent inside the city's name

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy
a rep is a representative or agent

explanation.surface: A head of state calls back an envoy posted in a foreign capital.
explanation.definitionFit: An emperor is the sovereign ruler of an empire, its supreme leader.

clue.text: Man in check with a pawn

parts.note: CH is chess notation for check
taken as written
P is chess notation for pawn

explanation.surface: A chess player threatening the king using a pawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' suggests a chess piece, but it is the definition: an ordinary fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: Chap is informal British for a man or fellow.

clue.text: Gardener gathering cheap crop ultimately for grain bin

indicators.note: gathering means collecting in, so the gardener's word surrounds the two letters

parts.note: a hoer is someone who works soil with a hoe

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so each of the two words gives only its last letter

parts.note: last letter of the word
last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A gardener collects a cheap harvest and stores it in a grain bin.
explanation.definitionFit: A hopper is a funnel-shaped container that feeds grain or seed out from the bottom.

clue.text: On the way out, kid charges on mud carelessly

indicators.note: the kid charges onto the mud and ends up within it
something done carelessly is messed up, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
to rib someone is to tease or kid them

explanation.surface: A young goat or child dashing recklessly across mud and about to fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' looks like a child or young goat, but it is the verb meaning tease.
explanation.definitionFit: Moribund means near death or in terminal decline, which is being on the way out.

clue.text: Toss stone

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to sway or pitch to and fro, as a ship does
second meaning: a mass of mineral matter

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like an instruction to throw a stone, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship tossed by waves is rocked, and a rock is a large stone.

clue.text: Monarch's family heading to gala

parts.note: kin are one's relatives

indicators.note: a heading sits at the top, so the next word gives only its first letter

parts.note: first letter of the word

explanation.surface: The royal family setting off to a gala event.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'has': the monarch is KIN with G added.
explanation.definitionFit: A king is a male sovereign, the monarch of a kingdom.

clue.text: Detective given power in intelligence deal

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector

indicators.note: in places the power symbol inside the word for intelligence

parts.note: sense means good judgement or intelligence
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A police detective gets authority in an intelligence-sharing arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deal' looks like a noun for an agreement but is the verb, as in dealing out cards.
explanation.definitionFit: To deal is to hand out shares, as cards are dealt, which is to dispense.

clue.text: Takes a break after Charlie reaches the top

indicators.note: after says the break comes second, placed behind the phonetic letter

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to rest is to take a break

explanation.surface: A climber called Charlie pauses for breath once at the summit.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay comes first and 'after Charlie' puts C in front of the break.
explanation.definitionFit: To crest a hill or wave is to reach its highest point.

clue.text: Perhaps seniors arranged departure

parts.note: e.g. means for example, perhaps

indicators.note: arranged means put into a new order, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Older people organising someone's leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: Egression is the act of going out, a formal word for departure or exit.

clue.text: Frequently scrubbed droopy tail of Rex

indicators.note: scrubbing out at frequent intervals removes every other letter, keeping the rest

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: A dog called Rex with a limp tail getting a good wash.
explanation.walkthrough: Rex sounds like a dog's name, but it is Latin for king, as in the abbreviation R on British coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal means belonging to a king, and rex is Latin for king.
